_comment: CELPIP Reading Part 1: Reading Correspondence. 6 multiple-choice questions about a message, then 5 blanks in a reply ({{id}} marks each blank). 'answer' is the index of the right option.

paragraphs: Hi Sam,

I'm sorry it has taken me so long to write. The last month has been a whirlwind! As you know, I started my new job at the aquarium on the first of June. I was hired to give tours to school groups, but the manager has already asked me to help train the summer volunteers as well. It's more work than I expected, but I'm really enjoying it. I spend every day explaining why sea turtles are so amazing, and I actually get paid for it!

Finding an apartment was harder than I thought it would be. Rents here have gone up a lot, and the first two places I liked were already taken by the time I called back. In the end, I found a small one-bedroom near the harbour. It's on the third floor of an old building with no elevator, so carrying my furniture up the stairs was quite an adventure. The good news is that I can walk to work in fifteen minutes, so I've sold my car.

Speaking of furniture, I need your advice. You always know where to find good deals. My living room is completely empty except for a few boxes. Should I buy a new sofa or look for a second-hand one online? I'd like something comfortable, but I don't want to spend more than about four hundred dollars.

Finally, I have a favour to ask. My cousin is getting married in Toronto on August 12, and I'll be away for five days. Would you be able to take care of my cat, Pepper, while I'm gone? I know you live a long way from here, but my brother could drive her to your place before I leave. Of course, I'll pay for her food and anything else she needs.
I hope you can come and visit me soon. The ocean views are worth the trip!

Take care,
Maya

It was great to hear from you! Your new job sounds perfect for you, and I'm not surprised the manager wants you to {{7}}. You've always been a great teacher.

About the sofa: since your budget is around {{8}}, I'd look online first. People often sell good sofas cheaply when they move. Just remember that your apartment is on the {{9}}, so ask the seller to help you carry it up!

items.title: A notice from the building manager

meta: From: Patricia Gomez, Building Manager, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Elevator replacement and parking changes
paragraphs: Dear Residents,

I am writing to let you know about important work that will take place in our building this fall. After more than thirty years of service, our elevator will be replaced with a new, faster model. The work will begin on Monday, October 6, and is expected to take four weeks.

While the elevator is out of service, residents will need to use the stairs. We understand that this will be difficult for some of you, especially residents on the upper floors. If you have a medical condition or a disability that makes using the stairs difficult, please contact the office by September 26. We will arrange help with carrying groceries and other items, and we can provide a list of nearby buildings that offer short-term rentals at reduced rates.

The contractor will need space to park two trucks and store equipment. For this reason, the six visitor parking spaces at the front of the building will be closed during the work. Visitors may park on Elm Street, where parking is free after 6 p.m. and on weekends. Residents' underground parking will not be affected.
The workers will be on site from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. Some noise is expected, especially during the first week, when the old elevator is removed. We apologize for the inconvenience.
Finally, we are looking for two volunteers to join a small committee that will help choose the design of the new elevator's interior. If you are interested, please reply to this email.
Thank you for your patience and understanding.

Sincerely,
Patricia Gomez

Dear Ms. Gomez,

Thank you for letting us know about the elevator replacement. I live on the ninth floor and recently had knee surgery, so climbing the stairs will be very hard for me. I'm writing before {{7}}, as you asked.

I would be grateful for help with my groceries. I would also like to see the list of {{8}}, as staying somewhere else for part of the month might be easier.

My daughter usually visits on Saturdays. I'll tell her to park on {{9}}, since the visitor spaces will be closed. Because parking there is {{10}} on weekends, it shouldn't be a problem for her.

Lastly, I would be happy to join the {{11}}. I worked as an interior designer for many years.

Best regards,
Daniel Okafor

paragraphs: Hi Priya,

As you know, my last day before parental leave is this Friday, and I'm very grateful that you've agreed to take over the Riverside Library project while I'm away. I wanted to put everything in one email so you have it in writing.

The most urgent task is the community survey. We've received about 300 responses so far, and the deadline is March 15. Please send a reminder to the mailing list next Monday; the message is already written and saved in the shared folder. Once the survey closes, the results need to go to Kenji in the data team, who has promised to prepare a summary by the end of March.

The second task is the reading-room renovation. The architect, Laura Kim, will send updated drawings next week. Our budget is $85,000, and her first estimate was about $10,000 over that. I suggested replacing the custom bookshelves with standard ones, which should close most of the gap. If she still can't get under budget, please talk to Martin before agreeing to anything, as he has to approve any extra spending.

You'll also be invited to the monthly meetings with the library board. They're usually on the first Thursday of the month at 4 p.m. The board members are friendly, but they like short presentations with clear numbers, so I'd keep your updates to five minutes.
I'll be checking my email occasionally, but please only contact me if something is really urgent. Martin knows the project well and can answer most questions.

Thanks again, and good luck!
Jordan
